newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 17.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* ITT is splitting itself into three companies and taking on about $2 billion in new debt.
* The Columbia/HCA inquiry by the federal government was expanded.
* Eastman Kodak reported second quater earnings that fell 16 percent.
* The FASB is proceeding with a controversial rule that would force companies to report the fair-market value of derivitives on their books.
* Consumer prices rose a scant 0.1 percent in June.
* Ford Motor posted a 33 percent gain in second quater net.
* Walt Disney 's ABC Television network is trying a new hardball tactic with Disney's animated-film rivals.
* Woolworth is expected to announce it will close the more than 400 stores of its F.W. Woolworth five-and-dime retail chain in the U.S.
* Stanley Works is expected to unveil a restructuring program that would cut as much as 25 percent of the tool manufacturers work force.
* BankAmerica led several major banks in reporting second quarter earnings that met or exceeded analysts expectations.
* Apple Computer posted a narrower-that-expected quarterly loss.
* As the Dow soars to new heights, more Wall Street strategists are running for cover.
